data.body:
SCOPE CORRECTION FROM THE OPERATOR — this resolves the S6 deadlock, and it changes what S6 must prove.

THE RULING: LLMs are non-deterministic. Expecting two runs to produce identical results is unrealistic
AND BEYOND THE SCOPE OF THIS EPIC. The epic's scope is to ensure THE SAME PAYLOADS REACH THE LLM and
THE LLM HAS THE SAME TOOLS AVAILABLE, regardless of model and provider. COMPARING MODELS AGAINST ONE
ANOTHER IS OUT OF SCOPE.

WHY THIS UNBLOCKS S6. The bar as written gated on model-behaviour equivalence — `parity.py` fails a run
on ANY nonzero `decision_flips` ("must be 0", no margin) and on verdict agreement below 0.95. Those
measure whether two DIFFERENT MODELS decide alike, which is now explicitly out of scope. The three
observed flips are genuine and reproducible, so no re-score removes them; under the old criteria S6
could never have been confirmed. Under the corrected scope that is not a failure at all — it is
expected non-determinism between different models.

CORROBORATION that the old bar was unsatisfiable, from data already paid for: ticket c403's measurement
found relation labels shifting on 6 of 12 ordered pairs BETWEEN BUILDS OF IDENTICAL CODE, with 1/12 and
3/12 within-build churn, reproduced independently twice. Different subsystem, so suggestive rather than
conclusive — but it shows verdict stability across runs is not a property this system has even holding
the model constant. A zero-flip bar across two different models presumed a determinism that does not
exist.

WHAT S6 MUST NOW PROVE — payload and tool parity, not verdict parity:
  * the request payload that reaches the provider is equivalent across providers for the same logical
    call (same messages, same system prompt, same tool definitions), modulo provider-required envelope
    differences;
  * the tool set available to the model is identical across providers;
  * provider routing is clean — a Bedrock-configured run makes no non-Bedrock calls;
  * any capability difference that legitimately alters the payload is EXPLICIT and recorded rather than
    silent.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN AGAINST THE CORRECTED SCOPE, from the run already performed:
  * PROVIDER-CLEAN ROUTING: zero non-Bedrock calls on 84/84 v2 case-runs, both slots, from the
    REBAR_USAGE_LOG per-call model tally. That is squarely in scope and it PASSED.
  * BEDROCK INVOKABILITY: attested for account 896586841071 / us-east-1.
  * A REAL CAPABILITY DIFFERENCE, correctly surfaced rather than hidden: `temperature=0` is refused on
    opus (`ValidationException: temperature is deprecated for this model`) and is already handled by the
    existing `supports_temperature: False` override — zero sampling rejections across 90 frontier v2
    case-runs. This is exactly the class of thing S6 SHOULD catch.

WHAT THE MEASURED VERDICT NUMBERS BECOME: informational evidence recorded on this ticket, NOT a gate.
They are retained because they are real and were expensive, and because the direction is worth knowing —
all three flips FAVOURED Bedrock (it caught a gold-BLOCK Anthropic missed and declined two gold-ADVISORY
cases Anthropic false-fired on). But they no longer determine whether S6 passes.

CONSEQUENTLY: no Anthropic-vs-Anthropic noise-floor run is needed, and no re-run of the paired eval is
needed. Both were only ever required to defend a criterion that is now out of scope.

STILL WORTH FIXING, on their own merits and NOT as S6 gates: 62ac (the false-accept metric computes
specificity but is consumed as an error rate, so it fails a run when the candidate improves) and 635f
(errored pairs scored as decision flips). Both are genuine correctness defects in code that exists,
independent of whether S6 gates on their output.

ACs 9 and 12 are being retargeted accordingly. This is a MATERIAL EDIT and it invalidates the certified
plan-review attestation; a fresh review-plan is required before claim/close.
